text: Team Moonlit sells an indie adventure game. Maya fronted a $400 art cost and must be repaid first from sales. After Maya is repaid, all revenue splits 40% to Maya, 30% to Arjun, 20% to Lina, and 10% to Dev. Once total net revenue hits $2,000, the split changes to an even 25% each. Hold 10% for refunds for 14 days, and only pay out when someone has at least $25.

Alex (Creator) and Apex Media launch an online course. Apex fronts $500 in ad spend which is recouped first. Thereafter, profits split 50% to Alex and 50% to Apex until $3,000 in net sales, after which Alex gets 60% and Apex gets 40%. A 10% reserve is held for student chargebacks.
Three hosts Sam, Chris, and Jordan share sponsorship income equally (33.33%, 33.33%, 33.34%). Equipment costs of $300 to Sam are paid back first. 10% reserve for sponsor clawbacks.
Single track digital sales: Artist gets 50%, Producer gets 30%, Audio Engineer gets 20%. Studio recording cost of $250 to Producer recouped first. Reserve 5%.
Four artists release an anthology comic. Printing fee of $1,200 to Elena repaid first. Remainder splits 35% Elena, 25% Marcus, 20% Chloe, 20% David. Reserve 15%. Minimum payout $20.
Client project billing: Agency Prime takes 55%, Senior Dev takes 30%, UI Designer takes 15%. Cloud hosting setup of $150 to Agency recouped first. 10% warranty holdback for 30 days.
Two co-founders Aaron and Beth split subscription proceeds 50/50. Beth's legal incorporation fee of $600 is reimbursed first. Reserve 10%.
Pay-per-view comedy ticket sales: Headliner gets 60%, Feature Act gets 25%, Emcee gets 15%. Streaming technician fee of $200 recouped to Headliner first.
Digital PDF sales for game module: Writer 40%, Illustrator 30%, Cartographer 20%, Layout Artist 10%. Upfront ISBN and proof fee $100 to Writer recouped first.
Channel merchandise sales: Channel Owner 65%, Video Editor 25%, Graphic Artist 10%. Sample manufacturing cost $350 repaid to Owner first.
Workshop ticket revenue: Lead Instructor 50%, Teaching Assistant 30%, Community Organizer 20%. Zoom webinar license $120 to Instructor recouped first.
Unity store asset pack sales: Modeler 45%, Texture Artist 35%, Rigging Artist 20%. Store listing fee $50 recouped first.
In-app purchase net receipts: Studio 70%, Publisher 30%. User acquisition ad test budget $2,000 recouped by Publisher first. After $10,000 net, split adjusts to Studio 80%, Publisher 20%.
Monthly track licensing: Composer gets 55%, Sound Engineer gets 45%. Mastering engineer fee $180 to Composer repaid first. 10% reserve.
A 5-person open source collective (DevA, DevB, DevC, DevD, DevE) splits all donation revenue equally (20% each). No upfront costs to repay. Standard 10% reserve.

We are making a joint project. Maya paid $300 for stuff. Pay her back, then split 60/40 between Maya and Liam. If people ask for refunds later, sort it out fairly. When we make good money after $1500, change to 50/50.
